neighbours.label: Inner pieces of a few biochemical names: 'ath' of glutathione, 'ulf' or 'ide' of disulfide, 'id' of guanidino: a list; other biochemistry stays quiet
fire: Cells use glutathione to neutralize free radicals.
Liver damage lowers glutathione in the blood.
Reduced glutathione protects the red cells.
Two cysteines form a disulfide bond in the protein.
Insulin chains are joined by a disulfide link.
The enzyme breaks disulfide bridges in hair.
Supplements of glutathione are popular in some countries.
Arginine carries a guanidino group on its side chain.
quiet: Cells use vitamin C to neutralize free radicals.
Liver damage lowers albumin in the blood.
Reduced iron protects the red cells.
Two cysteines form a strong bond in the protein.
Insulin chains are joined by a hydrogen link.
The enzyme breaks protein chains in hair.
Supplements of zinc are popular in some countries.
Arginine carries a positive charge on its side chain.

notes: Card: 'ath' x3, 'van' x3, 'ide' x2, 'ph' x2, 'ede' x2, 'ion' x2, 'id'. Probe: glutathione 'ath' 0.79-1.01, guanidino 'id' 0.77, disulfide 'ide' 0.51, 'ulf' 0.43; cysteine 0.03, hydrogen bonds 0.01, amino acid 0.00. Tokenizer checked. 'van', 'ph' on the card are not covered. All three are thiol or nitrogen-group chemistry, but I do not claim a chemical pattern.
